subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What policy should OpenClaw apply to non-operator-created recurring cron jobs that can dispatch agent turns and spend model quota?
rationale: Changing defaults, requiring confirmation, adding provenance, or enforcing spend limits affects compatibility, plugin contracts, provider spend policy, and security posture, so automation should not pick the permanent policy alone.

options.title: Stage provenance plus consent guardrails
options.body: Preserve explicit operator-created cron semantics, but require provenance and explicit activation or model/budget guardrails for plugin or agent-created recurring agentTurn jobs.

options.title: Default all new recurring cron jobs disabled
options.body: This maximizes spend safety but is likely to break existing users and bundled plugins that rely on scheduled jobs starting immediately.

options.title: Keep auto-enable and add observability only
options.body: This avoids compatibility churn but leaves the reported consent and runaway-spend failure mode mostly intact.

recommendation.title: Stage provenance plus consent guardrails
recommendation.body: Preserve explicit operator-created cron semantics, but require provenance and explicit activation or model/budget guardrails for plugin or agent-created recurring agentTurn jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail is recent merged cron and plugin workflow-seam work across the affected files.
